questions.prompt: Which statement best describes how evidence relates to a conclusion?

options.text: A conclusion is supported when it sounds familiar.
A conclusion is supported when the cited passage backs the specific claim.
A conclusion is supported when many sources repeat it.
A conclusion is supported when no source disagrees.

questions.prompt: Similarity between two passages is enough to show that one supports the other.
Select all that apply: which checks help when judging a claim against its source?

options.text: Read the passage the claim cites.
Count how many times the claim is repeated.
Compare the wording of the claim with the passage.
Trust the first summary you read.

questions.prompt: What should a learner do first when a conclusion needs checking?

options.text: Rewrite the conclusion in new words.
Return to the original passage and read it.

questions.prompt: Revisiting the original source is only useful before a conclusion is written.
In your own words, explain why a similar passage does not by itself establish support.
Describe what you would look for when you revisit an original source to check a conclusion.

key.explanation: Support means the cited passage backs the specific claim, not that the claim sounds familiar or is repeated.
Similarity by itself does not establish support; the passage has to back the claim.
Reading the cited passage and comparing its wording with the claim are the checks that show whether the claim is backed.
Learners can revisit the original evidence when checking a conclusion.
The original source stays useful after a conclusion is written, because it is what the conclusion is checked against.
A similar passage can resemble a claim without backing it, so the claim must be checked against what the passage says.
criteria: Says that similarity alone is not support
Says the claim has to be checked against the passage
key.model_answer: Two passages can look alike without one backing the other, so the claim has to be checked against what the cited passage actually says.

key.explanation: Revisiting the original source means reading what it says about the specific conclusion being checked.
criteria: Mentions returning to the original passage
Mentions comparing the passage with the conclusion
Mentions noting where the passage does not back the conclusion
key.model_answer: Return to the original passage, compare what it says with the conclusion, and note anywhere the passage does not back the conclusion.
